Patient account · 2024-10-21
actually i can answer those questions quite quickly as there isn't much. things that have helped: - nicergoline: old school vasodilator, noticeable improvement for the first 1.5 months, then effect slowly wore off. suggests neurological issues are at least partially circulation driven (see messages below) - MCT oil and possibly monolaurin: went from halfway bed bound to being more active - basic liposomal vitamins that i think raised my baseline energy - i'm taking a locally made probiotics and a liposomal pectin complex acting as a prebiotic, which have greatly improved my GI issues. went from dysbiosis and constant strong pain in both corners of the large intestines, slow motility and constipation to normal bowel movements and rare pains and rare constipation (so not fully healed yet). - KPV peptides did help with the constipation too but i went off them because was told they were not compatible with the above. - anti-histamine diet and in general lighter meals help: eating steak or anything more energy intensive to digest often triggered a brain burn. the energy requirement of digestion likely triggered dysautonomic symptoms -> cerebral blood flow issue nothing has really helped my severe brainfog and brain burns, sadly. peptides: have tried a few more other than KPV but unfortunately i forgot which. they didn't help my neurological issues though. will check and let you know which ones.

RapamycinStopped1 course

Single dose · The patient reports one 0.5 mg dose.

Clinical context

Severe patient-reported response · Curator assessment

A single 0.5 mg dose on 21 June 2025 preceded roughly ten days of recurring, exceptionally severe inflammatory/herx-like crashes. The patient retrospectively describes these as the most severe of the illness, subjectively so overwhelming he felt he might die. Severe CNS and upper-body fatigue developed, and brain burning and pressure returned. This is patient-reported severity and temporal association, not confirmation of life-threatening physiology or a proven inflammatory mechanism.

Source

Clinical context

Formulation · Curator assessment

The patient described this experimental nanocarrier formulation as intended to improve systemic or brain delivery, possibly via lymphatic uptake. Blood–brain barrier penetration and hepatic first-pass bypass were not independently measured; NC must not be treated as equivalent to every commercial liposome.

Dose reconciliation

The diary says approximately 400 mg elemental magnesium. The standard Magnosolv sachet label specifies 365 mg total magnesium (200 mg from oxide; 165 mg from carbonate). Do not rewrite the reported intake as exactly one sachet.

Clinical context

Unverified components

NADH was reported, but the full experimental mixture and any additional NAD+ precursors were not established. Do not infer a complete ingredient list or normalize contradictory dose dates.

S1:2024-10-25, S5:2024-10-21 and revision14 date clarification
Formulation · Curator assessment

The patient described this experimental nanocarrier formulation as intended to improve systemic or brain delivery, possibly via lymphatic uptake. Blood–brain barrier penetration and hepatic first-pass bypass were not independently measured; NC must not be treated as equivalent to every commercial liposome.

  • The S5 calendar diary dates NADH initiation to the evening of October 21, 2024, excess NADH to October 22, and the first documented physical crash to October 23. Magnesium followed NADH by about five hours. The exact onset across the night of October 22–23 is unresolved. The clinician identifies the October 23 “magnesium poisoning” entry as new deep muscle fatigue. The October 25 account describes progressive sleepiness and weakness, unusually good sleep, near-paralysis the next day, muscle cramps, and tingling without the usual pains. On November 2 the patient explicitly contrasted prior movement limitation during brain burning with fatigue now felt directly in the muscles, including when the brain burning was absent. · patient hypothesis; unconfirmed

BezisterimStopped1 course

Clinical context

Patient-reported fatigue deterioration · Curator assessment

During the late-2025 bezisterim trial, the patient reported markedly stronger CNS/brain fatigue and muscle fatigue (including nape and forearms), with a new lactate-like brain/forehead sensation, pressure behind the eyes and a major reduction in screen tolerance. A spore probiotic was being tried in the same period, so their individual causal contributions cannot be separated.

NC GABA (experimental nanocarrier)Stopped1 course

Clinical context

Formulation · Curator assessment

The patient described this experimental nanocarrier formulation as intended to improve systemic or brain delivery, possibly via lymphatic uptake. Blood–brain barrier penetration and hepatic first-pass bypass were not independently measured; NC must not be treated as equivalent to every commercial liposome.

Source

The formulation was intended to enter the CNS; BBB delivery is a reported intent, not a measured outcome. The February 2025 5–7.5 mL dose escalation belonged to this formulation.

Clinical context

Overall assessment · Curator assessment

No convincing sustained benefit after several months of use. Brief perceived improvements in 2024 may reflect spontaneous symptom fluctuations; the original diary still records them as temporal observations.

Source
S1-M62792 and 2024 S5 BEMER observations; reviewer 2026-11-21

Tolerin2 courses

Clinical context

No adverse events reported · Curator assessment

No adverse events were reported following either administration. This describes the patient report, not an independent safety determination.

Source
PZ60-TOLERIN:patient report; PubMed PMID 4603883 for historical name only
Unverified product authenticity · Curator assessment

The patient later suspected that the material might have been counterfeit or made without compliance with applicable manufacturing laws. No batch documentation, manufacturer, analysis or regulatory finding was supplied; this is a suspicion only.

Source
PZ60-TOLERIN:patient report; PubMed PMID 4603883 for historical name only
Unverified exposure hypothesis · Curator assessment

The patient later suspected possible heavy-metal or other toxic exposure from the injections. No exposure was confirmed and no causal relationship was established.

Source
PZ60-TOLERIN:patient report; PubMed PMID 4603883 for historical name only
Historical literature, not product evidence · Curator assessment

A 1974 local animal study refers to irradiated endotoxin as Tolerin. It does not authenticate or characterize the preparation administered here. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/4603883/

Source
PZ60-TOLERIN:patient report; PubMed PMID 4603883 for historical name only
